To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IMAT as measured by magnetic resonance imaging is a good surrogate for histological assessment of intermuscular fat.
MRI can be used to evaluate IMAT and that agreement between MRI and gold standard histology could be improved by adopting a more restrictive threshold to distinguish between muscle, IMAT and SAT.
IMAT can be measured by MRI, and that MRI‐derived IMAT measurements correlate well with histological evaluation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quantification of the IMAT in the erector spine muscle by MRI and histologic analysis.
the development of new tools for the assessment of IMAT, a new and emerging marker of metabolic and functional impairment.
the evaluation of IMAT by MRI and histopathology in a group of elderly subjects with different BMI.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

MRI is an accurate and reliable method to evaluate IMAT in vivo, and it could be a promising tool in the study of IMAT in different populations and in the evaluation of the effectiveness of therapeutic interventions.
MRI is a reliable method to assess fat infiltration of skeletal muscles, and that a more restrictive threshold for the discrimination between muscle and fat is required.
the MRI technique is a good tool to evaluate IMAT, and the agreement between MRI and the histological technique could be improved using a more restrictive cutoff between muscle and fat.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MRI could be used as a reliable method for IMAT quantification in the erector spinea muscle.

the use of MRI to evaluate IMAT is a valid method to be used in clinical practice, but it is necessary to consider that the threshold between muscle and adipose tissue should be reduced to improve the agreement with histological evaluation.
MRI could be a useful method for the evaluation of IMAT in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MRI can be used to assess IMAT and its relationship with metabolic syndrome and disability.

the agreement between histological evaluation and MRI is good and that MRI is a reliable method to quantify IMAT, which could be used in clinical studies to evaluate the impact of IMAT on muscle function and disability.
